chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Jameel, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Wheat with flour is like-for-like, and Sawiq with Sawiq is like-for-like, and barley with wheat is like-for-like, there is no problem with it.

key_terms.السَّوِيقُ: Sawiq (a type of roasted grain flour dish)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for exchanging wheat for flour or barley for wheat in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the application of the 'mithlan bi-mithl' (like-for-like) principle in *bay' al-gharar* (sale of uncertainty), specifically permitting the exchange of wheat for its processed form, flour, and barley for wheat, provided the measure is equal. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes between the intrinsic nature of the commodity and its processing, allowing such transactions to avoid the prohibition of *riba* (usury) inherent in unequal exchanges of the same genus. It reflects the practical legal reasoning of the Imams in facilitating trade while maintaining strict equity in weight and measure.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Jameel, from Muhammad Bin Muslim and Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
The wheat with the flour are the similar with a similar, and the Saweyq with the Saweyq is similar with similar, and the barley with the wheat is similar with similar, there is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 10. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Jamil from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah who have said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is permissible to exchange wheat with flour in equal measures and sawiq (mush) of wheat with mush and barley with wheat in equal measures, is not harmful.’”
